pitch: The hands-on guide of a manager who learned on the job: purpose, people, process, and the first years in the role.
center: The craft of the new manager
br: Facebook · age 25 · learning on the job

quiz: According to Julie Zhuo, what is a manager's job?
Getting better outcomes from a group of people working together
A manager is judged on what their team achieves, not on their personal output.
What are the manager's three levers?
Why the team exists, who does the work, and how it works together.
What is the situation of a manager promoted within their own team called?
The apprentice must change their relationship with former peers and learn to stop doing the work themselves.
Who does the one-on-one belong to?
It is the team member's time, to talk about what matters to them.
What does the author recommend before giving feedback on a project?
Many performance problems come from poorly expressed expectations.
Facing underperformance, what distinction does the author propose?
The solutions are very different: train and clarify, or understand what is blocking motivation.
How does Julie Zhuo approach impostor syndrome?
It's common: lean on your strengths and share your doubts
It goes away in a month
It proves you're not cut out for the job
It also affects very competent people, and never fully disappears.
What rule does she give about hiring?
Hire fast to relieve the team
Better to wait for the right candidate than fill a role with the wrong person.
